comparisons.peer_summary: Net charge-offs increased $1.2 billion to $3.7 billion in 2024 compared to 2023, while loans 30 days or more past due increased $219 million and those 90 days or more past due increased $177 million at December 31, 2024.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPM and BAC report an increase in credit card net charge-offs for 2024 compared to the prior year. JPM attributes this increase to the seasoning of recent vintages, credit normalization, and balance growth, while BAC reports a specific dollar increase of $1.2 billion to $3.7 billion and notes a corresponding increase in delinquencies (loans 30+ and 90+ days past due). Both disclosures reflect deterioration in credit quality for consumer credit cards during this period.

comparisons.peer_topic: Branded Cards net credit loss trends and drivers
comparisons.peer_summary: The Q4 2024 net credit loss rate in Branded Cards was stable quarter-over-quarter but increased year-over-year, driven by the maturation of recent vintages (previously delayed by pandemic stimulus) and macroeconomic pressures from inflation and interest rates affecting lower FICO band customers.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPM and C (Citigroup) identify the maturation or seasoning of recent loan vintages as a primary driver for increased net charge-offs (or net credit loss rates) in their credit card portfolios for 2024. JPM cites 'seasoning of vintages originated in recent years' as a cause for higher net charge-offs, while C explains that the net credit loss rate increased year-over-year 'primarily reflecting the continued maturation of multiple cards loan vintages originated in recent years.' Both also mention macroeconomic factors, with JPM citing 'credit normalization' and C citing 'macroeconomic pressures related to the elevated inflationary and interest rate environment.'

sentences.text: Net charge-offs increased for the year ended December 31, 2024 compared to the prior year reflecting the seasoning of vintages originated in recent years, credit normalization and balance growth.
The net credit loss rate increased year-over-year, primarily reflecting the continued maturation of multiple cards loan vintages originated in recent years.
In addition, the increase was driven by macroeconomic pressures related to the elevated inflationary and interest rate environment, with lower FICO band customers primarily driving the increase.

comparisons.peer_summary: Provision for credit losses increased to $1.54 billion in 2024 from $1.14 billion in 2023, primarily driven by net charge-offs in the credit card portfolio.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPM and GS attribute the increase in their respective provision for credit losses primarily to net charge-offs in the credit card portfolio. JPM reports $8.6 billion in net charge-offs driving the provision, while GS reports that its 2024 provision for credit losses ($1.54 billion) reflected net provisions related to the credit card portfolio 'primarily driven by net charge-offs.' Both disclosures highlight credit cards as the key driver of credit loss expense growth in 2024.
